*Dr Griggs, DVM at Forest West Aminal Clinic is a suberb veterinarian who earned the rank of the top of her class at Texas A&M Veterinary School. She stays current with the lastest discoveries, techniques and veterinary medications.
* Dr. Griggs has been the "vet in chief," tending to 7 of my canine children (over the years).
* Dr Griggs has great "clinic-side/bedside" manner. She speaks with respect to pet parents. Pet patients are treated with love and compassion.
* Staff at Forest West are friendly, excellent, highly experienced and loving, too. There's JoAnne, Millie, Amanda, Kendall and others--many of whom speak both English and Spanish. They are fabulous staff who gently and tirelessly nurse their patients like they are their own pets.
*Staff are dedicated to placing vaccine reminders and initiating follow-up visits. The staff receptionist cheerfully juggles scheduling to ensure everyone is scheduled.
* Staff facilitate ordering special food and meds for your pets delivered to your home.
*Forest West is an extremely popular clinic! Do not be surprised when you see the waiting room. It is often filled with friendly, satisfied, repeat pet parents. If needed, you can stay in your vehicle until your appointment time, once you check in with the recpetionist.
* Recent testimonial, my rescue, an older doggy gentleman, Toby was bitten by his doggy siblings. Despite fearing the worst, after 2-days of comprehensive treatment and affordable treatment fees, my Toby was on the road to recovery. Two weeks later, Toby is fully recovered. Dr. Griggs and her staff reached out daily via  phone calls with concern to ensure Toby was healing as intended.
*From the bottom of my heart, I am enternally grateful to the care provided by staff at the Forest West Clinic.
*Forest West is first class. I give them my highest endorsement, which would be much greater than five stars.

I truly love Dr. Griggs! She is always so attentive to my concerns! The staff is so friendly! I have tried several vet clinics, but Forest West Animal Clinic knocks it out of the park! My furry friends love to go see Dr Griggs!

Edited review:  1st review was after a couple visits with new kittens. This review is after a few more visits with my elderly cat. The vets are cool, but the real stars are their animal-loving, kind, very caring staff.

Original Review:
We tried this vet, that is no where close to us, because our regular vet is just too expensive.

We have two new kittens, took them to vet for their first vaccines and first exams.  I explained what tests and such we wanted... vet left and assistant came back with a list of the prices for each kitten of everything we wanted for approval before vet did anything else.... which we appreciate.

It cost us $480 for the two kittens to get their testings, vaccines, lime dip and medications....which was still cheaper than what my regular vet charges for "new kitten packages," plus we got extra stuff not included in our reg vet package.

As much as I will miss our last vet, we will continue to use Forest West.
I am very pleased with Forest West Animal Clinic they take great care of my Bootsy!

Dr. Griggs and her staff at Forest West Animal Clinic have been caring for our pups and cat for 9 years. Recently our older pup Steffi was limping and diagnosed with a torn ACL and required surgery. The procedure performed is called TPLO surgery and is very specialized and performed by Dr. Payne at the Forest West Clinic . The surgery was a great success and Steffi is now recovering very well, and will soon be able to return to her normal activities. Dr. Griggs is highly recommended for your loving pets needs and will be in the best of care along with other happy clients from Harris and surrounding counties. Dr. Griggs is undoubtedly the best veterinarian. Thank you so much for saving our baby.   🐾
Brian Ennemoser

I have to admit it's a good option in terms of price. Even though I was given one estimate when I called, and the final price was different when I arrived, I have no major complaints. However, as a suggestion, I think that before administering any other treatment to canine patients, the staff should provide a quote and explain to the owner what will be done, so they can decide whether to proceed with the entire treatment or just part of it.
The treatment from the doctor who injected my puppies and the young man who initially attended to us was undeniably good.

The reason I'm not giving them 5 stars is because the person who was in charge of administering the pills to my puppies, from the moment she walked in, seemed unenthusiastic about working with them.

In fact, she said something like, "It's too early," because my puppies were nervous and wouldn't open their mouths to take their pills. Furthermore, I noticed how much difficulty she had opening my puppies' mouths because her nails were extremely long, preventing her from interacting with them and doing her job properly. As a suggestion, anyone working in any medical field should NOT have such long nails, especially if they handle living beings and medications.

Update: I recently returned to the clinic for my puppies' second vaccination, and it was truly impressive to see that they had taken into account the suggestions I mentioned in my previous comment. The doctor was kind, and the rest of the staff who cared for my puppies were simply wonderful. They are people who love what they do. They get a 10/10!

This is typically my main vet and I had no issues with them until I took a pet in for a checkup. They knew something was immediately wrong and preformed a check-up the same day. X-rays, blood tests, etc. They took the issue seriously, however..

The results were pretty conclusively cancer. The vet who gave me the news comforted me and said she'd send the results to an oncologist to get a definitive diagnosis and other relevant information. She said this could take anywhere from a few hours to a few weeks depending on their availability. I got a lot of medications to make her more comfortable and was sent home.

I went home to deal with the news of my dog having cancer and waited for a call about the results. Nothing ever came. I never got a single phone call from them after. I waited a few days, but after about a week I called and inquired about results. The receptionist always told me the vet in charge would call me back when she was in the office.

Every time I called I was told she either wasn't there or if she was there, I would get told she'd call me when she had free time. This happened over the course of around 2-3 weeks, with my eventually calling every day. One time I called and asked again and the receptionist said the results weren't even in the system. I didn't know if they didn't come back yet, or if they weren't put into their computers, or what. They gave me absolutely no information every single time I called. I had no idea what her prognosis was so everyday was scary. I eventually decided to just show up in person to demand results in the morning but the day of my dog passed away next to me at 3am, probably in a considerable amount of pain. I had no idea how far long she was so I didn't know if euthanize was a good idea. Not like they would've told me since they just never had any information for me.

This vet is usually wonderful but if anything life threatening happens I'm going somewhere else. There was so much negligence with my dogs life. I would've liked to get SOME information, even a timeframe of how much longer I had with her. I am sadly not the only person in these reviews to have a similar experience.
